bib.title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed for lineage only; per-domain MMLU Tables 16-18 scanned, not recorded cell by cell.

question: Does few-shot learning on knowledge-intensive tasks require storing knowledge in model parameters, or can a jointly pre-trained retrieval-augmented model match much larger LLMs with few examples?
hypothesis: Retrieval may be crucial to endow models with few-shot capabilities, and memorisation can be decoupled from generalisation by outsourcing it to a non-parametric index.
contributions: A thorough study on how to design and train retrieval-augmented language models, with a focus on downstream few-shot learning and sample efficiency.
Atlas, a retrieval-augmented language model whose few-shot abilities emerge at lower scale than standard LLMs.
An exploration of fine-tuning strategies to efficiently adapt both the retriever and the language model.
Few-shot state of the art on NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA and FEVER, and results on par with models with 15x more parameters on MMLU.
Full-dataset fine-tuning state of the art on NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA and 5 KILT tasks.
A product-quantised index gives comparable performance with a 5x memory reduction.

method.summary: Atlas pairs a Contriever dual-encoder retriever (BERT-base) with a T5 Fusion-in-Decoder reader, pre-trains both jointly on unlabelled text with a masked-language-modelling task and a retriever loss derived from the reader (Perplexity Distillation), then fine-tunes per task on few or many examples. Ablations at T5-XL (3B) pick the loss, pretext task, index content and retriever fine-tuning strategy; the final family spans 770M to 11B reader sizes.
method.task: Knowledge-intensive tasks (open-domain QA, fact checking, KILT, MMLU) in text-to-text form, few-shot and full-data

datasets.name: Wikipedia dump (Dec 20, 2021), index and pretraining
datasets.source: Wikipedia; lists and infoboxes kept and linearized; articles split by section, long sections into equal passages under 200 words

datasets.name: Common Crawl 2020-10 via CCNet
datasets.preprocessing: Gopher-style filtering on document length, average word length, alphanumeric ratio, repeated tokens

datasets.name: KILT (NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, zsRE, T-REx, AIDA, WoW, FEVER)
datasets.split: 64-shot, 1024-shot and full train; hidden test via leaderboard; dev in Table 20
datasets.preprocessing: instances needing knowledge outside the August 2019 Wikipedia dump removed

datasets.name: MMLU
datasets.split: zero-shot; 5-shot per domain; multi-task 5-shot (285 examples); transfer with 95k examples from MCTest, RACE, ARC, OBQA

datasets.name: TempLAMA-derived time-sensitive cloze set
datasets.split: questions whose answer differs between 2017 and 2020

models.name: Atlas
models.architecture: T5 Fusion-in-Decoder reader plus Contriever dual-encoder retriever
models.context: query plus passages truncated to 384 tokens (QA)

models.name: Closed-book T5
models.init_from: same T5 as the matching Atlas

other.pretraining: MLM for 10K steps on the same data as Atlas

other.note: numbers quoted from the original papers; prompted, not fine-tuned

training.objective: Reader: seq2seq generation of masked spans (MLM pretext, 15% masking, mean span 3 tokens). Retriever: KL between retriever top-K distribution and the reader posterior (Perplexity Distillation); ADist, EMDR2 and LOOP also compared.
training.lr: pretraining ablation: 1e-4 reader, 1e-5 retriever; few-shot KILT/QA fine-tuning: 4e-5 both; MMLU: (5e-5, 1e-5)
training.warmup: 1,000 steps (pretraining); 5 steps (few-shot fine-tuning); 500 iterations (KILT full fine-tuning)
training.batch_size: 64 pretraining ablation; 128 final models; 32 few-shot fine-tuning; 64 full-data and MMLU
training.steps: 10,000 pretraining iterations; 64-shot QA 30 steps; ablation fine-tuning 50 (64-shot) and 200 (1024-shot); full-data 5k steps; MMLU per Table 14
training.regularisation: answer-option permutation in MMLU training; pretraining passage filtered from its own retrieved set
training.compute: Table 7: Atlas 3.5e22 train FLOPS vs GPT-3 3.1e23; pretraining compute dominated by T5 pretraining
training.seeds: MMLU 5-shot run 5 times for variance (std 0.5 overall); main-table numbers use the first run; other experiments single run

other.index_refresh: every 1,000 steps in ablation (index recomputed 10 times, ~30% overhead); final models every 2,500 steps with re-ranking of top-100; full QA fine-tuning every 500 steps for first 1,000 then every 2k
other.retriever_finetune: query-side for small data, standard for larger; MMLU full setting uses top-128 reranking
other.mmlu_hparams: Table 14: retriever temperature 0.1; 5-shot steps 64/32/16 for 770M/3B/11B; multitask max steps 2000/500/250; full/transfer 5000/2000/2000
other.fewshot_model_selection: KILT 64-shot: evaluated every 5 steps, best on dev; NQ 64-shot: model after 30 steps

inference.decoding: greedy decoding (QA, KILT); MMLU picks the argmax over the logits of letters A-D
inference.samples: single run per setting; MMLU 5-shot repeated 5 times in Appendix
inference.prompting: template 'question: {q} answer: [MASK_0]'; MMLU template with options (A)-(D)
inference.retrieval: top-k from a dense index over Wikipedia and CCNet (387M passages for MMLU); exact search sharded over GPUs; PQ compression studied

parameters.mmlu_debias: 4 cyclic answer permutations (4x inference) or all 24

other.index_memory: 49 GB (Wikipedia) and 587 GB (combined) at fp16; PQ to 4 GB and 50 GB

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: MMLU micro-averaged across 57 domains; FEVER; AIDA, T-REx, zsRE

eval.protocol: Few-shot Atlas fine-tuned; most baselines prompted. Single run except MMLU variance check. No development set assumed for MMLU 5-shot (hyperparameters from RACE).

prompts.text: question: {question text} options: (A) {answer 1 text} (B) {answer 2 text} (C) {answer 3 text} (D) {answer 4 text} answer: [MASK_0]

limits: The headline comparison is fine-tuning (Atlas) against in-context prompting (PaLM, Chinchilla, Gopher, GPT-3): the method differs as well as the size (Table 8 and 9 captions).
Chinchilla at 5-shot MMLU (67.5) beats Atlas (47.9); the MMLU claim is only against GPT-3 and Gopher-scale comparisons.
The retriever-loss and other ablations are single runs at 3B on three tasks, without error bars; only MMLU 5-shot was repeated (std 0.5).
Main-table results quote the first run only; the variance run used a slightly different index.
The temporal test is small (806 questions) and templated; the closed-book T5 comparison is on data predating 2020.
The authors concede KILT results are not directly comparable with the original NQ, TQA, FEVER versions.
MMLU leakage was estimated for CCNet only, and larger-corpus LLMs probably see more.
Hardware, wall-clock and seeds are not reported; the 11B result depends on an index of up to 587 GB at fp16.

terms.definition: Train the retriever to predict how much each document would improve the language model perplexity of the output, via KL between retriever and reader-posterior distributions over the top-K documents.
Fix the document encoder and train only the query encoder, so document embeddings need no refresh.
Relevance of each document is how much worse the output log probability gets when that document is removed from the top-k set.

lineage.note: Joint training of retriever and generator

figures.caption: We introduce Atlas, a retrieval-augmented language model that exhibits strong few-shot performance on knowledge tasks, and uses retrieval during both pre-training and fine-tuning.
figures.why: Shows one model serving MLM pretraining and QA/fact-checking fine-tuning.

figures.caption: MMLU Retrieval Analysis: sources of retrieved passages, answer occurrence by number of passages, and accuracy by answer frequency.
figures.why: Shows 85% of retrieved passages come from CCNet and accuracy rises from 55% to 77% with answer frequency.

figures.caption: Index Compression: Atlas-3B 64-shot NQ performance as a function of index size for different levels of quantisation.
figures.why: Shows the memory-accuracy trade-off of product quantisation.

figures.caption: Comparison to state-of-the-art on question answering; for the 64-shot setting our model uses fine-tuning, while the other models use prompting.
figures.why: The headline comparison and its method caveat.

code.snippet: p_k ∝ p_LM(a | d_k, q) = exp(log p_LM(a | d_k, q)) / Σ_i exp(log p_LM(a | d_i, q)); minimise KL against p_retr(d|q) = exp(s(d,q)/θ) / Σ_k exp(s(d_k,q)/θ)
